The checksums for both sources are provided and non-trivial, indicating an intent to verify integrity. The use of `zig fetch` is appropriate in this context, as it is part of the Zig build system's dependency management and operates on a pre-downloaded, checksum-verified `.tar.gz` file listed in `source` and excluded from extraction via `noextract`. There is no use of `eval`, `curl|bash`, or any unverified network access during build or package phases.

The build steps correctly set `ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR` to a local directory to ensure reproducibility and isolation. The `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions perform standard operations: compiling with Zig, running tests, and installing binaries and documentation into the package directory. All installed files are from the verified source tree, and no system modifications or post-install hooks are included. The package depends only on `glibc` and `openssh`, which are reasonable for its functionality.

No obfuscated code, suspicious downloads, or dangerous runtime behaviors are present. The secondary dependency from `https://github.com/meszmate/zigzag` is fetched in a controlled manner and not executed directly — it is used as a library. While the source uses HTTPS URLs and pinned tags (not git branches), there is no evidence of supply-chain tampering or malicious activity. The packaging adheres to standard AUR practices and poses no security risk.
</details>
